exercise1.prompt: A grouped summary laid out as a grid.

hiddenCases.name: one subject and one year is a single cell
the grid has a column per distinct year

exercise1.hint: index is what goes down the side, columns is what goes across the top, values is what fills the cells. The shape is distinct subjects by distinct years.

questions.prompt: What does the index argument of pivot_table control?
questions.explain: index is the row key and columns is the top. Swapping them transposes the grid, which is the exercise's wrong answer.

questions.prompt: A subject and year pair with no rows becomes what cell?
questions.explain: A grid has every cell whether the data did or not, so absent combinations arrive as gaps. Whether a gap should read as 0 is your decision.

questions.prompt: How does a pivot table relate to a group-by?
choices: It is the same summary laid out as a grid
questions.explain: Same split-apply-combine underneath. The difference is the shape of the answer and therefore how easy it is to read.
